title: Pope Damasus II (151º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the Duchy of Bavaria.

title: Pope St. Leo IX LEO Nonus (152º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the Duchy of Swabia. In 1054, the mutual excommunications of Leo IX's legate, cardinal Humbert of Silva Candida, and Patriarch Michael I Cerularius of Constantinople started the East–West Schism. The mutual anathematizations were rescinded by Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I in 1964.

title: Pope Victor II (153º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the Duchy of Swabia.

title: Pope Stephen IX (154º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the Duchy of Lorraine. Last German pope until Benedict XVI(2005–2013). Sometimes called Stephen X. Member of the Order of Saint Benedict.

title: Pope Nicholas II (155º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the County of Savoy. Was of French ethnicity. Designated the College of Cardinals as the sole body of pope electors in the bull In nomine Domini(1059).

title: Pope Alexander II (156º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Citizen of the Free Commune of Milan. Authorized the Norman conquest of England.

title: Pope St. Gregory VII (157º): Canossa, Reform & Church vs. State
sourceNotes: Subject of the March of Tuscany. Was of Lombard ethnicity. Initiated the Gregorian Reforms. Restricted the use of the papal title to the bishop of Rome. Member of the Order of Saint Benedict. Political struggle with Emperor Henry IV, who had to go to Canossa(1077).

title: Pope Bl. Victor III (158º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the Duchy of Benevento. Was of Lombard ethnicity. Member of the Order of Saint Benedict. Called the Synod of Benevento (1087), condemning lay investiture.

title: Pope Bl. Urban II (159º): Crusades — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Subject of the Kingdom of France. Preached and started the First Crusade. Member of the Order of Saint Benedict.

title: Pope Paschal II (160º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the March of Tuscany. Was of Lombard ethnicity. Member of the Order of Saint Benedict. Ordered the building of the basilica of Santi Quattro Coronati.

title: Pope Gelasius II (161º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the Duchy of Gaeta. Member of the Order of Saint Benedict.

title: Pope Callixtus II (162º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the County of Burgundy. Was of French ethnicity. Convened the First Council of the Lateran(1123).

title: Pope Honorius II (163º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Canon Regular of the Lateran. Approved the Knights Templar as a military order (1128).

title: Pope Innocent II (164º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Canon Regular of the Lateran. Convened the Second Council of the Lateran(1139).

title: Pope Celestine II (165º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
birthPlace: Città di Castello, Sacro Roman Empire
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope Lucius II (166º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Canon Regular of San Frediano.

title: Pope Bl. Eugene III (167º): Crusades — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Citizen of the Republic of Pisa. Member of the Order of Cistercians. Announced the Second Crusade.

title: Pope Anastasius IV (168º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope Adrian IV (169º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the Kingdom of England. The only English (Anglo-Saxon) pope; purportedly granted Ireland to King Henry II of England. Canon Regular of Saint-Ruf monastery.

title: Pope Alexander III (170º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the March of Tuscany. Convened the Third Council of the Lateran(1179).

title: Pope Lucius III (171º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject of the March of Tuscany.

title: Pope Urban III (172º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Was of Italian ethnicity. In the 21st century, Cuggiono is a small Italian town and comune in the Metropolitan City of Milan.

title: Pope Gregory VIII (173º): Crusades — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Canon Regular Premonstratense. Proposed the Third Crusade.

title: Pope Clement III (174º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope Celestine III (175º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Papal motto: Perfice gressus meos in semitis Tuis ("Going in Thy path"). Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Confirmed the statutes of the Teutonic Knights as a military order.

title: Pope Innocent III (176º): Lateran IV, Power & Medieval Papacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Convened the Fourth Council of the Lateran(1215). Initiated the Fourth Crusade but later distanced himself from it and threatened its participants with excommunication when its leadership abandoned their focus on conquest of the Holy Land and instead decided to sack Christian cities. Endorsed the Franciscan Order.

title: Pope Honorius III (177º): Crusades — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Initiated the Fifth Crusade. Approved several religious and tertiary orders.

title: Pope Gregory IX (178º): Crusades — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Initiated the inquisition in France and endorsed the Northern Crusades.

title: Pope Celestine IV (179º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Citizen of the Free Commune of Milan. Died before coronation.

title: Pope Innocent IV (180º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Citizen of the Republic of Genoa. Convened the First Council of Lyon(1245). Issued the bull Ad extirpanda(1252), permitting the torture of heretics.
